Structures from the ACS Fall 2025 poster (Simiyu and Smith): the primary ozonide from C2H4 + O3 falls apart to CH2OO + H2CO. Every number comes from the runs listed on the last slide.

slides.title: Ozonolysis makes CH₂OO hot enough to leave the well
slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Motivation · ozonolysis

Ozonolysis makes CH₂OO hot enough to leave the well

C₂H₄ + O₃ forms CH₂OO with up to 48 kcal/mol (about 2.1 eV) above its minimum, the dashed line.

That is above the barriers out of the well, so part of the CH₂OO reacts before collisions can cool it.

Hot molecules sample geometries far from the minimum, where a harmonic or well-only surface does not hold.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 2 · energies: HEAT-345(Q), Nguyen et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 119, 5524 (2015); figure: Simiyu & Smith, ACS Fall 2025
slides.notes: Energies relative to the CH2OO minimum, from the HEAT-345(Q) study of Nguyen, Lee, Matthews, McCarthy and Stanton (J. Phys. Chem. A 2015, 119, 5524-5533), as drawn on our ACS Fall 2025 poster. Ozonolysis releases a broad distribution of energy into CH2OO: some is collisionally stabilized, some decays promptly (to dioxirane over TS 1, and to other products). 48 kcal/mol is about 2.1 eV, comparable to the O-O dissociation region of the NEVPT2 surface later in the deck and above the 0.4-1.8 eV window of the new CCSD(T) shell. That is the regime the surface must handle for ozonolysis-energy IR and branching. Two cautions from Kuwata's 2024 perspective (J. Phys. Chem. A 128, 7331): Nguyen et al. attribute nearly all the OH from ethene ozonolysis to primary-ozonide diradicals rather than to CH2OO, and a significant fraction of small Criegees is formed cold or collisionally stabilized (Kroll et al. 2001).

slides.title: CH₂OO is the test case; larger Criegees are the goal
slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Motivation · prediction

CH₂OO is the test case; larger Criegees are the goal

CH₂OO

Smallest Criegee, with the most data to test against: IR bands, UV spectrum, photodissociation products

Test the method here

CH₃CHOO

syn and anti conformers, told apart by IR, react at very different rates

Lin et al., Nat. Commun. 6, 7012 (2015)

MVK-oxide

Four carbons, from isoprene ozonolysis: conformers, few spectra, kinetics leaning on theory

Vansco et al., PNAS 117, 9733 (2020)

Unimolecular decay to OH depends on how much energy the Criegee carries (Lester & Klippenstein, Acc. Chem. Res. 51, 978, 2018). As molecules grow, experiments thin out: predictions need a surface we trust at high energy, checked first where the data are rich.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 3
slides.notes: The pipeline is meant to carry over: build the surface from a cheap multireference method everywhere plus a coupled-cluster correction where it is valid, check it against spectroscopy, then run dynamics. CH2OO is where every step can be checked. References: Lin, Huang, Wang et al., Nature Communications 6, 7012 (2015), syn- and anti-CH3CHOO by step-scan IR; Vansco et al., PNAS 117, 9733-9740 (2020), isoprene-derived methyl vinyl ketone oxide; Lester and Klippenstein, Acc. Chem. Res. 51, 978 (2018), prompt and thermal decay of Criegee intermediates to OH.

First study: IR emission following photolysis of CH₂I₂ in the presence of O₂, which forms CH₂OO with 13 kJ/mol excess energy above the zero point: the 13 kJ/mol condition in the dynamics later in this deck.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 4 · energy increases down the table
slides.notes: IR absorption: Su, Huang, Witek and Lee, Science 2013, 340, 174, step-scan FTIR of CH2OO from CH2I + O2; bands at 1435, 1286, 1241, 908 and 848 cm-1. IR emission: time-resolved FTIR emission from highly vibrationally excited molecules, as in Smith, Nikow, Ma, Wilhelm, Han, Sharma, Bowman and Dai, JACS 2014, 136, 1682 (super energy transfer collisions) and Smith, Nikow, Wilhelm and Dai, J. Phys. Chem. A 2023, 127, 8782 (hot acetylene relaxation via vinylidene). Emission from hot CH2OO itself is a target: we have not found a published spectrum. First study: CH2I2 photolysis in the presence of O2 (CH2I + O2 gives CH2OO + I) with CH2OO carrying 13 kJ/mol above its zero point; the ir stage's 13 kJ/mol microcanonical runs are the computed counterpart. One surface has to pass all three probes, because ozonolysis-energy dynamics crosses all three regions. UV photolysis: Beames, Liu, Lu and Lester, JACS 2012, 134, 20045 (UV spectrum, prompt dissociation near 335 nm); Samanta, Beames, Lester and Subotnik, J. Chem. Phys. 2014, 141, doi 10.1063/1.4894746 (quantum dynamics on coupled singlet states); Esposito et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2021, 125, doi 10.1021/acs.jpca.1c03643 (velocity map imaging and trajectories: O(1D) + H2CO and O(3P) + H2CO channels through conical intersections). Methods for Criegee UV spectra are reviewed by Kuwata, J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 7331 (next slide).

slides.title: What a Criegee model must get right (Kuwata, 2024)
slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Motivation · state of the art

What a Criegee model must get right (Kuwata, 2024)

Kuwata’s perspectivewhat it means for this project
Conformation decides the fate: syn-alkyl CIs shift H to vinyl hydroperoxides and OH; CH₂OO and anti CIs close to dioxirane or react with waterthe method has to carry over to conformers of CH₃CHOO and MVK-oxide
Ground-state reactivity: single-reference CCSD(T) with transition state theory agrees with experimentsupports CCSD(T) for the well and the shell
UV spectra need multireference methods with large active spaces and at least second-order dynamic correlation; EOM-CCSD is 0.2 eV too highour NEVPT2 network uses (8,6): test it against (12,10) before the UV benchmark
CH₂OO UV structure comes from the B/C avoided crossing near r(O–O) 2.1 Å, modelled in r(O–O), ∠COO and r(C–O)the same coordinates as our surface; needs the B and C states and their coupling: the diabatic network
Roaming in vinyl hydroperoxide decay needs static and dynamic correlation and variational rate theorydynamics on an ML surface can treat it directly, as trajectories on a global ab initio surface did for complex-forming H + HCCH collisions seen by IR emission (Smith et al., JACS 136, 1682, 2014)

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 5 · K. T. Kuwata, J. Phys. Chem. A 128, 7331–7345 (2024), doi 10.1021/acs.jpca.4c04517
slides.notes: Kuwata, "Computational Modeling of the Conformation-Dependent Atmospheric Reactivity of Criegee Intermediates," J. Phys. Chem. A 2024, 128, 7331-7345 (Perspective). Points used here: (1) syn-alkyl and syn-vinyl CIs isomerize quickly to vinyl hydroperoxides or dioxoles; CH2OO and anti CIs prefer dioxirane closure or bimolecular reaction (water, SO2). (2) Single-reference methods with conventional TST and Eckart tunneling have matched experiment for ground-state reactivity. (3) For the CH2OO B-X spectrum, MRCI+Q-F12b(18,14) gives vertical excitation 3.75-3.83 eV, EOM-CCSD 4.01 eV (too high: no static correlation); CASPT2(12,10) beat (10,8) and MRCI(10,8) (McCoy et al.), so a larger active space matters more than the level of dynamic correlation; TDDFT is about 0.7 eV too blue. For MVK-oxide smaller active spaces, including (8,6), shifted lambda-max 50-100 nm red. (4) Nikoobakht and Koppel trace the vibrational structure to the B/C avoided crossing near R(O-O) 2.1 A, using R(O-O), theta(COO) and R(C-O): the coordinates of our 3-D surface. (5) Roaming of OH in vinyl hydroperoxide decay needs multireference electronic structure and variational TST. Our related precedent: Smith, Nikow, Ma, Wilhelm, Han, Sharma, Bowman and Dai, 'Chemical Activation through Super Energy Transfer Collisions,' J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 1682-1685: hot H atoms (about 60 kcal/mol) form a transient complex with HCCH, and about 10% of collisions leave up to 70% of the energy in acetylene vibration, seen by time-resolved IR emission and reproduced by quasi-classical trajectories on a global ab initio potential (Bowman group). Long-lived complexes on a flat region of the surface are the same dynamical regime as roaming, and the same IR-emission and trajectory tools apply. Also noted: Nguyen et al. attribute almost all OH from ethene ozonolysis to primary-ozonide diradicals, not to CH2OO.

slides.title: Spectra from dynamics on a learned surface
slides.section: Why: hot Criegees from ozonolysis, larger Criegees, and the spectroscopy that tests a surface
slides.html:
Approach · ACS Fall 2025

Spectra from dynamics on a learned surface

Surface = energy + Δ + dipole. Dynamics on it, then the Fourier transform of the dipole autocorrelation gives a spectrum to compare with experiment.

Since the poster, for CH₂OO:

a quasi-diabatic NEVPT2 network for all four states, a CCSD(T) grid for the well, quantum levels to check the band positions, and Δ-learning to join them.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 6 · B. N. Simiyu and J. M. Smith, poster, ACS Fall 2025 National Meeting
slides.notes: Figure 1 of the poster: Simiyu and Smith, "Vibrational spectral prediction of transient species using machine learning potential energy surfaces," ACS Fall 2025 (Temple University; Hylleraas Centre, University of Oslo). There the surfaces were trained on importance-sampled points from DFT (B3LYP/cc-pVTZ) direct dynamics, with CCSD(T) and a Delta correction; the example panels show a small test molecule (O-H stretch and torsion). The rest of this deck is what changed for CH2OO and why.

slides.title: Four findings since the hot-molecule IR work
slides.section: Where the project stands and why the surface had to change
slides.html:
Summary

Four findings since the hot-molecule IR work

1 · The surface set the band positions

The NN ensemble could not fix the curvature at the minimum, and the SA4 reference data scattered 5–50 meV between points.

2 · A clean grid fixes the data

State-specific CASSCF+NEVPT2 grid: fit residual 0.3 meV. Quantum O–O fundamental 937 cm⁻¹ (3-D), 944 (4-D); experiment 908.

3 · The band shape is rotational

Each trajectory gives a P/R doublet at ν₀ ± ω_rot; 160 trajectories give a smooth envelope like experiment’s.

4 · CCSD(T) gets the anharmonicity

4-D CCSD(T): O–O shift −28 (VPT2 −24). With aug-cc-pVTZ harmonics, O–O 907 and C–O 1281 vs 908 and 1286.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 7
slides.notes: One line each. The rest of the deck backs these up in order: why the surface had to change, the clean grid and DVR, the rotational contour, then 4-D, basis and NEVPT2.

slides.title: Why the neural-network surface could not set band positions
slides.section: Where the project stands and why the surface had to change
slides.html:
Starting point

Why the neural-network surface could not set band positions

28 meV

ensemble members disagree at the minimum

±0.015 Å

scatter of the members’ minima

A frequency depends on meV over hundredths of an Å. An energy fit with tens-of-meV errors leaves that curvature to chance; low-energy weighting made it worse.

Step 1: a polynomial fitted to the well data (cubic, 454 points) as the spectroscopy surface.

Step 2: CH₂ restraint springs stiffened ×9. At ×1 their modes (970, 1171 cm⁻¹) mixed with O–O, pushed it to 905 and took intensity.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 8
slides.notes: The 905 cm-1 match in the first polynomial run was partly the spring artifact. With restraint_scale = 9 the springs sit at 1793 cm-1 and above and carry no intensity.

The data problem

The SA4 reference data could not pin the O–O curvature

Cause

The top root of the four-state average (9–11 eV up) jumps by up to 2.5 eV between neighbours. The averaged orbitals change with it and S0 moves 5–50 meV.

Tracking compares S1–S2 only, so it cannot see this.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 9
slides.notes: Fits that reproduce the data well disagree by 200+ cm-1 on the O-O harmonic with the SA4 data. On the state-specific grid (shaded) fits within 1 meV agree to about 10 cm-1.

slides.title: Quantum levels on the same surface, by DVR
slides.section: A clean ground-state grid and quantum levels on it
slides.html:
New stage · vib_levels

Quantum levels on the same surface, by DVR

H = −(ħ²/2) Σ ∂ᵢ Gij(q) ∂ⱼ + V(q)

  • G: inverse kinetic metric, translations and rotations removed (J = 0)
  • Sinc DVR: V diagonal on the grid; kinetic term Σ Dᵢᵀ G Dⱼ
  • 28³ grid (3-D) or 20⁴ (4-D); lowest 16 states in 5–30 s
  • Assigned by overlap with harmonic states; intensity ν |⟨0|μ|v⟩|²

Built-in checks

Harmonic test on the grid: 0.01 cm⁻¹

Wavefunction density at the grid edge

Harmonic frequencies over polynomial orders and windows

Flags levels “not reliable” when the polynomial dives outside the data

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 11
slides.notes: Method write-up: docs/dvr_note.html. Code: diabml/vibdvr.py and diabml/workflow/vib_levels.py. Colbert and Miller, J. Chem. Phys. 96, 1982 (1992). The Podolsky extrapotential is left out; it is nearly constant over the well.

slides.title: NEVPT2 stiffens the outer O–O wall; CASSCF does not
slides.section: Beyond the 3-D model: CH2 scissor, basis set, NEVPT2
slides.html:
Open issue · run 29_aug

NEVPT2 stiffens the outer O–O wall; CASSCF does not

Beyond r(O–O) ≈ 1.42 Å the NEVPT2 correction curves up, most at short C–O. Present in both bases.

The aug minimum sits close to it, so O–O v = 1 reaches it: harmonic spread 860–910, levels flagged not reliable.

Not a missing orbital: the (8,6) space keeps O–O σ/σ* along the whole cut. Next slide: tested against CCSD(T) and FIC-NEVPT2.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 17 · second differences along r(O–O) at ∠COO 117.7°
slides.notes: 29_aug: 1331 points, 106 min. One point had its two starts disagree by 74 mEh, another sign that the active space is strained at the edges. The ORCA outputs show the six active orbitals unchanged in character along the cut: three pi, the O-O sigma/sigma* pair and the terminal O lone pair. The next slide gives the method check.

slides.title: Only NEVPT2 turns up; CCSD(T) stays smooth
slides.section: Beyond the 3-D model: CH2 scissor, basis set, NEVPT2
slides.html:
Method check · 33 points of 29_aug, aug-cc-pVDZ

Only NEVPT2 turns up; CCSD(T) stays smooth

Not the contraction: FIC-NEVPT2 follows SC-NEVPT2 within 1–2 eV/Å²

Not the minimum: at 1.368 Å all agree, 26.5 / 26.5 / 26.6 eV/Å²

CCSD(T) T1 0.036–0.051: above the 0.02 guide; read with care

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 18 · ∠COO 117.7°; 66 ORCA runs, 1.3 min
slides.notes: Upturn from the curvature minimum to the last point: SC-NEVPT2 +10.8 and FIC +11.3 eV/A2 at r(C-O) 1.244 A; +9.4 and +10.0 at 1.269 A; none at 1.294 A. CCSD(T) and CASSCF fall monotonically in all three cuts. The active orbitals keep the same character along the cut (three pi, O-O sigma and sigma*, terminal O lone pair), so the (8,6) space does contain sigma/sigma*: the upturn is NEVPT2 on this reference where long O-O meets short C-O, the direction of CH2O + O. The T1 values say CCSD(T) is not fully safe either, but its curve behaves as a stretching bond should.

slides.title: The upturn came from state-specific orbitals, not state mixing
slides.section: Beyond the 3-D model: CH2 scissor, basis set, NEVPT2

Method check · QD-NEVPT2 added

The upturn came from state-specific orbitals, not state mixing

curvature (eV/Å²), r(C–O) 1.244 Å1.4281.4581.488
SC-NEVPT2, state-specific23.127.933.9
SC-NEVPT2, SA3 orbitals15.312.49.9
QD-NEVPT2, 3 states15.212.410.0
CCSD(T)16.512.89.9
  • QD ≈ SC on SA3 orbitals: state mixing negligible
  • QD S1–S0 gap 4.7 → 2.9 eV along the cuts: no surface hopping in the well
  • SA3 has its own jump at short O–O (~240 meV vs CCSD(T) ~90)

Verdict: CCSD(T) for the ground-state well. For the NEVPT2 excited states: state-averaged orbitals, tracked including the top root.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 19 · run 29_aug, method_cut with qd_nroots = 3
slides.notes: The same pattern holds at r(C-O) 1.269 A; at 1.294 A no method turns up. The SA3 jump sits between r(O-O) 1.278 and 1.308 A (1.308 and 1.338 A at r(C-O) 1.294): another averaged solution, the same kind of switch that spoiled the SA4 data. State-averaged orbitals behave better toward dissociation, the direction that matters for ozonolysis and branching.

slides.title: Correct the cheap global surface only where CCSD(T) can be trusted
slides.section: Toward one surface: Δ-learning on the diabatic network
slides.html:
Toward one surface · the Δ idea

Correct the cheap global surface only where CCSD(T) can be trusted

The network keeps every state and coupling from NEVPT2. CCSD(T) fixes the ground-state well.

Δ is added to every diagonal element, so the gaps, eigenvectors and hopping are unchanged.

A switch w turns Δ off where the states crowd together.

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 24 · data: 24_spec and 29_aug, r(C–O) 1.27 Å
slides.notes: Written for an undergraduate audience. Panel 1: NEVPT2 is multireference, so it describes all four states out to CH2O + O(1D), but at cc-pVDZ and with SA4 noise. CCSD(T) is single-reference: accurate in the well (T1 0.03-0.07) and not valid where the states crowd together. Panel 2: Delta = CCSD(T) minus the network's NEVPT2 ground state at the same geometries. Panel 3: a smooth model of Delta (polynomial or GP), multiplied by a switch w that is 1 in the well and 0 past 1.75 A. Panel 5 is why this is safe for dynamics with surface hopping: adding the same number to every diagonal element of the diabatic matrix shifts all adiabatic energies equally and leaves the mixing (eigenvectors) and therefore the nonadiabatic couplings alone. The switch range and the cubic Delta are illustrative; the next slide shows what the switch costs in force.

slides.title: A ramp, not a barrier, and most of it need not be switched
slides.section: Toward one surface: Δ-learning on the diabatic network
slides.html:
Toward one surface · what the switch costs

A ramp, not a barrier, and most of it need not be switched

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 25 · 29_aug method check: CCSD(T) and NEVPT2, both aug-cc-pVDZ
slides.notes: The Delta figure plots Delta in meV over a short O-O range, which makes the switch look like a cliff. On the surface's own scale (panel A) it removes about 0.13-0.15 eV (3 kcal/mol) over 0.2 A, while the bond climbs about 2 eV. What trajectories feel is force (panel B): up to about 1.2 eV/A added where the bond force is about 3.3 eV/A, roughly a third, which is enough to change how fast a hot O-O bond stretches. The fix (panel C): most of Delta here is not CCSD(T) versus NEVPT2 at all. The method cut has state-specific NEVPT2 and CCSD(T) in the same aug-cc-pVDZ basis, and their difference is under 5 meV in the well (it grows to about 30 meV at 1.52 A, partly the state-specific upturn). The rest, about 100 meV, is basis and orbital (cc-pVDZ SA4 to aug-cc-pVDZ), and both sides of that are multireference, so it is valid at any O-O and needs no switch. Plan: learn Delta_MR from a NEVPT2 aug-cc-pVDZ cut out to dissociation (about 20 points, still to be measured; the dotted line is a placeholder), apply it everywhere, and switch only Delta_CC. A wider switch alone does not help much here because Delta is still changing at the edge of the data.

slides.title: A Gaussian process says where it is unsure; a polynomial does not
slides.section: Toward one surface: Δ-learning on the diabatic network
slides.html:
Toward one surface · fitting Δ

A Gaussian process says where it is unsure; a polynomial does not

J. M. Smith · Temple University · 26 · GP: diabml.gpdelta, Matérn 5/2, fitted length scale 0.18 Å
slides.notes: Same 11 Delta points as the Delta figure. A polynomial is one global formula: it fits the points well but carries its trend past the data, here diving to -400 meV by 1.7 A, and gives no warning. A GP builds the curve from the data with a kernel that sets the smoothness; with a zero prior mean it relaxes back to no correction over about one length scale (0.18 A here) and its error band widens as it does. That error band comes from the same fit: it drives the choice of the next shell batches (largest sigma) and, by drawing posterior samples, gives error bars on the fundamentals. Limits: sigma is interpolation error only, not the error of CCSD(T); it must be checked on held-out batches (shell_check does). The GP's own relaxation to zero is a soft switch, but its length scale is learned from the well, so the explicit switch w stays. Use: polynomial for the dense, smooth well data in vib_levels; GP for Delta on the network across the sparse shell.
